name: get the intended change approved before implementing it
about: The gate before any code, and this step's `gate` field is where that sentence goes: whoever writes this step into a plan writes it there by hand, in words about THIS job, because a definition cannot author one and a step left with an empty `gate` reads to every later reader as a step needing nobody. Write the two-section summary IN YOUR OWN CHAT — that is what he reads — in the format `sb presets design-gate` prints, then `sb block`. The preset owns the format; this step owns the two sections it fills: FIRST the Scope & Objectives, then the Change Contract. He answers approve, or rejects with changes — and ON A REJECTION YOU REDO THE DESIGN WORK, re-derive the scope, re-infer the objectives, rebuild the contract, then summarise and block again, because editing the wording of a summary he rejected answers a different question from the one he asked. When he approves, put the FULL approved text in the step's `output` field, because that is what the PR comment dumps, and EMPTY THE `gate` FIELD as you tick — a gate left on a step that is already done is a defect `validate` reports. This step comes BEFORE implementation and is an early root of the plan, whatever order it was added in — that is where naming it puts it. Obliges `review`, where the contract you got approved is checked against what was built, and that obligation is never omitted. A trivially small change skips this with the reason in `why`: a behavioural contract for a typo is a block nobody wants. COMBINED, AND RECORDED AS AN IDENTITY. This one sign-off covers the selected solution, the plan revision and the change contract together, and it is the SHAPED path's alone — a DIRECT change has no plan and no contract and never gets one, going straight to the work. When he approves, the approval goes into the change record as an identity — `change.approval`, carrying the plan revision it covers and the digest of the contract — so that `review` and landing compare that identity rather than re-reading the wording, and implementation is presented as sanctioned only once it is recorded.
